name: Glaucoma Guardian
tagline: Diagnosis, Monitoring, and Management of Glaucoma
description: A 15-episode series covering every clinical decision point in glaucoma care — from IOP and gonioscopy through OCT and visual fields to first-line therapy and surgical referral.

episodes.title: Glaucoma Pathophysiology: The Only Modifiable Risk Factor is IOP
episodes.description: The mechanical and vascular theories of glaucomatous optic neuropathy, why lowering IOP is the only proven treatment, and target pressure setting.

episodes.title: Intraocular Pressure: Measurement, Diurnal Curve, and Peak IOP
episodes.description: Why a single IOP reading is insufficient, the diurnal fluctuation in glaucoma, and when to admit a patient for a diurnal curve.

episodes.title: Gonioscopy in Glaucoma: Open, Closed, Plateau, and Secondary Angles
episodes.description: The angle grading systems (Shaffer, Spaeth), identifying plateau iris, pigment dispersion in the angle, and PAS vs neovascularisation.

episodes.title: Optic Nerve Evaluation: Cup-to-Disc, RNFL Defects, and Disc Haemorrhages
episodes.description: Documenting the optic nerve with the 5R framework, recognising focal notching, splinter haemorrhages, and bayonetting vessels.

episodes.title: Visual Field Testing in Glaucoma: 24-2, 10-2, and the Glaucoma Hemifield Test
episodes.description: Choosing the right strategy (SITA-Standard vs SITA-Fast), recognising glaucomatous field defects, and distinguishing true progression from noise.

episodes.title: OCT in Glaucoma: RNFL Thickness, GCC, and the Progression Graph
episodes.description: Interpreting the OCT printout, distinguishing red disease from true glaucoma, and using the progression analysis to confirm change over time.

episodes.title: Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma: Diagnostic Criteria and Risk Stratification
episodes.description: When ocular hypertension becomes POAG, the OHTS trial findings, and risk calculators that guide the decision to treat.

episodes.title: Normal-Tension Glaucoma: Diagnosis, Systemic Associations, and Treatment
episodes.description: How NTG differs from POAG, the role of nocturnal blood pressure dips and sleep apnoea, and the more aggressive target IOP.

episodes.title: Acute Angle-Closure Crisis: Recognition and Immediate Management
episodes.description: The acute ACG presentation, immediate treatment protocol (pilocarpine, mannitol, acetazolamide), and laser peripheral iridotomy timing.

episodes.title: Secondary Glaucomas: Pigmentary, Pseudoexfoliative, and Uveitic
episodes.description: Distinguishing pigment dispersion syndrome, PEX material on the pupil, and steroid-induced IOP spikes — each with a different management algorithm.

episodes.title: Prostaglandin Analogues: First-Line Medical Therapy and Side Effects
episodes.description: Why PGAs are first-line (once daily, potent, low systemic side effects), managing conjunctival hyperaemia and the prostaglandin-associated periorbitopathy.

episodes.title: Beta-Blockers, CAIs, and Alpha-Agonists: Adjunctive Medical Therapy
episodes.description: Adding a second agent when the PGA is insufficient, the systemic contraindications of beta-blockers, and the role of fixed-combination drops.

episodes.title: Selective Laser Trabeculoplasty: Indications, Technique, and Outcomes
episodes.description: When SLT is the right first choice, the 360 vs 180 degree debate, and the typical IOP reduction and duration of effect.

episodes.title: When to Refer for Glaucoma Surgery: Trabeculectomy, Tubes, and MIGS
episodes.description: The surgical ladder from MIGS (iStent, Kahook) to trabeculectomy to tube shunts, and what the optometrist must know about post-op co-management.

episodes.title: Glaucoma Follow-Up Schedule: Frequency, Testing Battery, and Compliance
episodes.description: How often to see the stable vs progressive patient, which tests at each visit, and strategies to improve drop compliance in chronic disease.
